chunks: The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Qasim al-Siqqal that he wrote to him:

O our Master, a man vowed to fast one day for Allah, and during that day, intercourse with his wife occurred upon him, incurring the expiation (kaffarah). He asked for a ruling, and he was answered: He must fast one day in place of the vowed day, and free a believing slave.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who breaks his vow to fast by having intercourse with his wife?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the expiation (kaffarah) for breaking a fast vow through sexual intercourse is distinct from the obligation to fulfill the vow itself. Consequently, the individual must fast one day to compensate for the missed vowed day and additionally free a believing slave as the specific penalty for the act of intercourse. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the debt of the vow (wajib al-nadr) and the penalty for its breach due to major acts.
